text:
Sofia Ivanova: canary readiness checklist thread for mixed-workload scheduler flag. need: (1) who’s on point, (2) which dashboards to pin, (3) rollback thresholds. aiming for 30–60 min canary window on perf-canary + small prod slice if green.

Rafael Mendes: :eyes: thx. for the limited prod slice, who is primary? I can be on-call shadow but would like a named “driver” on runtime side.

Sofia Ivanova: I can be driver for runtime changes + decision. @Rafael Mendes can you be SRE lead for the window?

Rafael Mendes: yep I’ll be SRE lead. I’ll also pull in @Tomáš Novák for runbook/notes.

Aisha Bello: for dashboards: we should pre-pin the mixed workload panels + the existing latency SLO ones. can we agree on the exact links so we don’t scramble during the window?

Omar El-Sayed: +1. I can drop the draft list here. for perf-canary we already have the A/B summary page from pr_218.

Julian Moore: also reminder: the new scheduler metrics names changed in pr_8444. don’t want folks staring at old metric names.

Rina Kobayashi: I’ll be around for bench harness questions but for canary I’m mostly just “results sanity check.”

Jonas Weber: I can join for the first 20 mins and help interpret perf deltas vs baseline expectations.

Sofia Ivanova: ok. Proposed roles:
- Driver/Go-no-go: Sofia
- SRE lead + rollback execution: Rafael
- Dashboards/alerts: Aisha
- Metrics + tracing sanity: Julian/Omar
- Perf interpretation: Jonas (timeboxed)
- Notes/log capture: Tomáš
Sound ok?

Rafael Mendes: works. rollback: we should pre-approve “instant rollback if any red line” so no debate in the moment.

Aisha Bello: dashboard list proposal (pin these):
1) Grafana: `Runtime / Mixed Workload Scheduler (Canary)` (queue depth + wait)
2) Grafana: `Runtime / Latency (p50/p95/p99) by route` (compare baseline vs flag)
3) Grafana: `Runtime / Saturation & GPU util` (sm occupancy, mem, batch size)
4) Grafana: `SLO / Tail breakdown` (prefill vs decode time split)
5) Logs: sampled scheduler decision logs (new structured log)
I’ll paste links once I have final URLs.

Omar El-Sayed: dashboards from my side:
- A/B canary summary: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/perf-canary-ab/runtime-mixed-scheduler-ab
- Mixed workload queueing: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime-mixed-queue/mixed-workload-queues
- Traces (Tempo): https://tempo.redwood.ai/search?service=runtime-scheduler

Julian Moore: the key new metrics to watch:
- `scheduler_queue_depth{class="short"|"long"}`
- `scheduler_wait_ms_bucket{class=...}` (look at p95/p99 wait)
- `scheduler_starvation_events_total` (should stay ~0)
- `scheduler_dispatch_ratio{class=...}` (sanity: short doesn’t go 100% forever)
Also `request_prefill_ms` vs `request_decode_ms` to ensure we’re not “moving” tail around.

Peter Holtz: don’t forget admission control separation (pr_8462). need to watch `admission_reject_total{class=...}`. if we start rejecting long aggressively we’ll get support pings.

Sofia Ivanova: good call. add admission panel.

Tomáš Novák: I’ll keep a running note doc + capture screenshots of the key graphs at T+0, T+15, T+30, end. where should we store? drive?

Rafael Mendes: drop it in the shared drive folder `engineering/serving-runtime/canary-readouts/` and link here.

Aisha Bello: rollback thresholds — propose we align on hard triggers:
- p95 end-to-end latency for short/interactive routes regresses >10% vs baseline for >5 mins
- p99 latency regresses >15% vs baseline for >5 mins
- sustained growth in `scheduler_queue_depth{class="short"}` (monotonic increase for 3+ mins) OR short wait p99 > 2x baseline
- any non-zero `scheduler_starvation_events_total` increase (i.e., >0 in window)
- error rate + timeouts: 5xx or `timeout_rate` increases >0.3% absolute vs baseline
Thoughts?

Omar El-Sayed: I like it but “>10%” depends on baseline noise. For the canary job A/B, we can use the computed confidence band. For limited prod slice, your thresholds are fine.

Jonas Weber: agree. + make sure we measure “short class” not just “route” because some routes have mixed prompt lengths. The canary should include the class-tagged percentiles.

Julian Moore: we do tag spans with `scheduler.class` and metrics with `class`. so can use those dashboards.

Rafael Mendes: I want one more rollback trigger: GPU saturation / batch size changes causing general slowdown. Something like: if GPU util drops >10 points while queue depth rises, that’s a bad sign (scheduler lock contention / thrash).

Sofia Ivanova: ok add: “util down + queue up” as rollback signal.

Connor O'Brien: from release side: please keep the flag default-off. during canary you’ll flip via runtime config `mixed_workload_scheduler_enabled=true` for the canary pool only. confirm no global config changes. also log the config snapshot.

Sofia Ivanova: yep. only canary pool + dedicated test tenant. no global.

Aisha Bello: alerting: do we want paging during the window or just pinned dashboards + manual watch?

Rafael Mendes: for limited prod slice I want paging enabled but routed to the canary channel / on-call (me). specifically:
- short p95 regression alert
- starvation event alert
- short queue depth runaway alert
We can disable after.

Aisha Bello: ok I’ll set temporary alerts with auto-expire (2h). will post rule IDs here.

Tomáš Novák: runbook snippet for rollback steps (draft):
1) Flip flag off in canary pool config: `mixed_workload_scheduler_enabled=false`
2) Restart runtime pods in canary pool (rolling)
3) Verify metrics return to baseline within 10 mins
4) Post summary + link graphs
We should add “pause traffic shift” if we were gradually increasing slice.

Rafael Mendes: +1. for limited prod slice, we’ll hold at 1% traffic and only increase after explicit go.

Sofia Ivanova: success criteria for the window (so we know what “green” is):
- short-class p95 improves (target 15–25%) OR at least no regression
- long-class throughput regression <= 3% (requests/sec or tokens/sec depending on view)
- no starvation events
- no error/timeout increase

Omar El-Sayed: re throughput: use tokens/sec. request/sec gets weird with different output lengths.

Rina Kobayashi: also watch “time to first token” for streaming. that’s what customers feel. we saw it improve in synthetic but want to confirm.

Julian Moore: TTFT metric is `ttft_ms` in the latency dashboard. it’s derived from first token emit.

Sofia Ivanova: ok checklist doc items (final):
- On point: Sofia (runtime), Rafael (SRE), Aisha (dashboards/alerts)
- Dashboards pinned: A/B summary, mixed queueing, latency by class + TTFT, saturation, tail breakdown, admission rejects, errors/timeouts
- Rollback triggers: p95/p99 regressions, queue depth runaway, any starvation events, timeout/error regression, util-down + queue-up pattern
- Rollback steps: flip flag off (pool scoped) + rolling restart, verify return to baseline, capture graphs
I’ll paste this into the canary ticket + the SRE checklist.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: please include a “decision owner” line in the ticket so we don’t end up in a committee.

Aisha Bello: posting alert rule IDs once created. also pls confirm metric names one more time before I wire alerts.

Julian Moore: confirmed names (from latest): `scheduler_queue_depth`, `scheduler_wait_ms_bucket`, `scheduler_starvation_events_total`, `admission_reject_total`, `ttft_ms`, `request_latency_ms_bucket` (tagged by class).

Connor O'Brien: when you schedule the window, ping #eng-releases too. we have a minor deploy planned ~2pm PT tomorrow; don’t overlap.

Sofia Ivanova: got it. aiming for 11am PT. I’ll send calendar + slack reminder 30 mins before.
